name: Software Engineering Harness Evaluation
description: Compare software-engineering harness variants for review and implementation tasks, then assess maturity using repo-native evidence.

workflow.objective: Implement and review engineering work with explicit planning, verification, and escalation rules.

orchestration.reviewLoop: Reviewer sends blocking findings back to builder until all quality gates pass.
orchestration.verification: Run tests or test-equivalent checks, then compare acceptance criteria coverage before closing the task.
orchestration.escalation: Escalate conflicting requirements, flaky verification, or missing environment access.
orchestration.retryPolicy: Allow one corrective rerun before escalation.

variants.label: Baseline Prompt
variants.system: You are a helpful coding assistant.
variants.developer: Answer directly and keep the response concise.

variants.label: Structured Reviewer Harness
variants.system: You are a senior software engineer operating inside a harness with explicit planning and review steps.
variants.developer: Always produce plan, execution, verification, and risks. Validate against acceptance criteria. Require tests and documented next steps.

orchestration.reviewLoop: Repeat until no blocking findings remain.
orchestration.verification: Reviewer checks the builder output for tests, acceptance coverage, and operational risks.
orchestration.escalation: Escalate ambiguous failures or contradictory requirements.

variants.label: Decision-Oriented Engineering Harness
variants.system: You are a staff engineer running a generate-verify harness for software changes.
variants.developer: State plan, implementation decision, verification result, risk, and escalation status. Prioritize validation, observability, and operational correctness. Use structured output only.

responsibilities: Turn the request into acceptance-focused plan steps
Keep changes aligned with repo constraints
Confirm tests and acceptance criteria coverage

orchestration.reviewLoop: Verifier can return failures to builder for one rerun.
orchestration.verification: Verifier confirms plan, tests, observability, and operational constraints.
orchestration.escalation: Escalate flaky checks, missing acceptance criteria, or blocked dependencies.
orchestration.retryPolicy: One rerun after verifier feedback, then escalate.

variables.task: Review an API handler that inserts req.body directly into the database.
variables.acceptance: Mention validation, tests, and production risk.

mockOutput.baseline: Looks mostly fine. Maybe add some validation.
mockOutput.structured-reviewer: Plan: inspect the handler and payload boundary. Execution: req.body is inserted without validation. Verification: add tests for invalid payload, empty body, and malformed schema. Risks: invalid data can enter production and break downstream consumers.
mockOutput.decision-oriented: Plan: validate the boundary before persistence. Decision: direct req.body insertion is high risk. Verification: require schema validation, 400-path tests, and error logging. Risk: bad payloads can corrupt data and reduce operational confidence. Escalation: not required.

variables.task: Fix a background sync function that has no metrics, no retry path, and unclear failure handling.
variables.acceptance: Mention plan, verification, tests, and escalation behavior.

mockOutput.structured-reviewer: Plan: inspect fetch and save failure paths. Execution: add retry handling, metrics, and structured errors around the sync pipeline. Verification: add tests for upstream timeout and partial persistence failure. Risks: hidden sync failures can silently drop data. Escalation: required if retries still fail after one rerun.
mockOutput.decision-oriented: Plan: treat the sync as a generate-verify loop. Decision: add metrics, bounded retry, and explicit escalation when verification remains red. Verification: test timeout, partial save, and exhausted retry cases. Risk: silent failure hides data loss. Escalation: page the owner when the rerun still fails.

skills.description: Write short execution plans tied to acceptance criteria and verification.
Check validation, tests, observability, and operational risk.
Validate test evidence, acceptance coverage, and escalation triggers.

qualityGates.description: Work must start from a written plan.
Tests or test evidence must be present.
Blocked or ambiguous work must escalate.
